password.description: Password aging controls for new accounts: maximum days between changes, minimum days between changes, and days warning before expiry.

pass_max_days.description: Maximum number of days a password may be used.

pass_min_days.description: Minimum number of days allowed between password changes.

pass_warn_age.description: Number of days warning given before password expiry.

ranges.description: UID/GID ranges: normal users (uid_min–uid_max, gid_min–gid_max) vs system accounts (sys_uid_min–sys_uid_max, sys_gid_min–sys_gid_max).

uid_min.description: First normal user UID to assign (inclusive).

uid_max.description: Last normal user UID to assign (inclusive).

gid_min.description: First normal group GID to assign (inclusive).

gid_max.description: Last normal group GID to assign (inclusive).

defaults.description: User creation defaults: login shell, home directory location, initial umask, user private group behavior, mail spool, and additional default groups.

def_shell.description: Default shell for new users (full path).

def_home.description: Base directory for new users' home directories (prefix).

umask.description: Default umask for file creation by new users (octal string).

usergroups_enab.description: Whether to create a private group for each new user (true = enable UPG).

spool_dir.description: Base directory for user mail spool files.

items.description: Name of a group to add new users to by default.

limits.description: Login session controls: max failed login attempts and timeout before re-prompting.

login_retries.description: Maximum number of failed login attempts before exit.

login_timeout.description: Seconds before login prompt times out (0 = no timeout).

logging.description: Login audit logging: whether to maintain a failure log, log unknown failures, and log successful logins.

faillog_enab.description: Enable faillog(5) logging of failed logins.

log_unknown_fail.description: Log unknown usernames in faillog (helps detect brute-force attempts).

log_ok_logins.description: Log successful logins in the faillog file (not recommended for security).
